description: Commit the exit from build (build=true) or buy (build=false) mode. Engine-side this signals the VMEventType.TSOUserLeaveBuildBuy event, which the server uses to snapshot a thumbnail. Prerequisite: you are the lot owner (handler-side; server-side Verify is permissive but the event is only meaningful for owner/builder flows). Effect: a lot thumbnail save is queued server-side — not directly observable via perception; may show in server logs. Cost: free. Wire: VMNetLeaveBuildBuyCmd { Build }. OQ-8: this is NOT a gate — skipping leave-build-buy has no functional consequence for the agent; architecture mutations take effect via their own VMNet*Cmd PDUs independent of this marker.
call_signatures: cf $CF leave-build-buy                                                                                  # owner-only; build=true by default
cf $CF leave-build-buy --build false                                                                    # leaving buy mode instead of build
common_mistakes: Non-owner → ok:false (this is a consistency check — server itself returns true in Verify).
build=true is default (leaving build mode); pass build=false to commit leaving buy mode.
perception_hints: Am I the owner? perception.lot.owner_is_me — architecture ops are owner-only
Your position (to anchor where to build): perception.avatar.position.x, .y (tile coords — arch ops accept tile coords directly, unlike walk-to)
Walls/floors are NOT exposed in perception — use query-architecture (test helper) if you need pre/post state
refuse_conditions: caller is not lot owner → returns ok:false with 'caller is not lot owner (owner_id=..., me=...)'
required tile coords (x, y) missing → returns ok:false with '<verb> requires x, y ...'
width/height/length <= 0 where specified → returns ok:false with specific bounds error
